title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Researcher agent for GCC users
summary: The briefing accurately reports the launched GCC roadmap item and explicitly presents Microsoft's conflicting availability, blocking and compliance guidance. The controls are supported; minor corrections should complete the web-search navigation and name the Graph baseline property that changes web search.

claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.quote: The Bing search service operates separately from Microsoft 365 and has different data-handling practices.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[0].scope
claims.claim: The Agent 365 actions page disables Edit users for Researcher and directs administrators to tenant-wide Block.
claims.quote: For the Researcher and Analyst agents, the Edit users panel is disabled. To manage their availability, block the agent for the entire tenant by using the Block action in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Manage agents page conflicts with blocking guidance by saying Researcher does not fall under agent-related settings.
claims.quote: Researcher and Analyst are part of the core Copilot chat experience and will not fall under any agent-related settings.

claims.claim: Web search is configured through Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > Create > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot.
claims.quote:
Under Customization, select Policy Management.
On the Policy configurations page, select Create.
On the Start with the basics page, enter a name (required) and a description (optional), then select Next.
claims.fix: Complete the path in controls[1].ui and its rendered row as 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot'. The existing Cloud Policy source supplies the omitted heading and name-entry page; the cited web-search article supplies the final policy.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can set web search using applyOnce mode.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor object that runs periodically in the background at a scheduled frequency to detect configuration drift in monitorOnly mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[1].note and the rendered row: 'The request body sets mode to applyOnce and includes a baseline resource with resourceType microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch, resourceVersion 1 and properties.value: "0" enables web search in both experiences, "1" disables it in both, and "2" disables Work mode web search, including Researcher.' The resource and property values are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-copilot-resources#allowwebsearch-resource-type.

claims.claim: The Graph web-search route uses preview applyOnce functionality.
claims.quote:
Apply a baseline once with applyOnce (preview)
A monitor in applyOnce mode applies its baseline in a background job on behalf of the administrator who created or updated it.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy UI supports user and group targeting for web search.
claims.quote: This policy allows IT admins to either turn on or turn off web search for users or user groups across the tenant they manage

claims.claim: TCM supports these Copilot settings only in tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: The 20 Copilot resources are Office Cloud Policy Service (OCPS) settings. TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: TCM operations fail for a target setting configured in a group-level policy.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the least-privileged signed-in user role for Copilot TCM remediation and applyOnce.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.claim: User license assignment is available at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page.
Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to.
In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps.
Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with UserId, AddLicenses containing SkuId, and empty RemoveLicenses assigns a license.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Disabling Copilot Work mode web search also disables web search in Researcher.
claims.quote: If the IT admin chooses the Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat option, web search in Researcher and Cowork in Microsoft Copilot will be disabled.

claims.claim: The non-federal GCC Anthropic page currently documents model-picker availability only in Copilot Chat in the Microsoft Copilot app and on the web.
claims.quote: Currently, those models appear as an option in the dropdown model picker only in Copilot Chat in the Microsoft Copilot app and on the web.

claims.claim: Claude models are unavailable for federal GCC customers and all GCC High and DoD customers.
claims.quote: Claude models aren't available for federal customers in GCC or for any customers in GCC High and Department of Defense (DoD) environments.
